analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר. The words that follow begin God’s direct speech with יִשְׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם, “Let the waters swarm.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים (“and God said”), the third-person masculine singular verb identifies אֱלֹהִים as the single speaker who commands the waters to teem with life.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a root article for שרצ with the Qal verb שָׁרַץ and its sense in Genesis 1:20.
draft.definition: Of waters, to teem with living creatures.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 1:20 the waters are commanded to teem. Genesis 1:21 repeats the verb when it describes the living creatures with which the waters teemed.

analysis.evidence: הַמַּיִם, “the waters,” is the plural subject of יִשְׁרְצוּ. The cognate noun שֶׁרֶץ names what the waters are to teem with, and נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה identifies the swarm as living creatures. וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים introduces the clause as God's spoken command.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural, with jussive force in God's command. The prefix יִ־ and ending ־וּ mark the inflection.
analysis.sense: Of waters, to teem with living creatures.

draft.change: Add the root שרצ with the collective noun שֶׁרֶץ and its related Qal verb שָׁרַץ.
draft.definition: Living creatures that swarm, taken collectively.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 1:20, שֶׁרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה names the swarm of living creatures with which the waters are to teem.

analysis.evidence: In יִשְׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם שֶׁרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, the waters are commanded to teem. The noun שֶׁרֶץ echoes the verb יִשְׁרְצוּ, and the following נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה identifies what makes up the swarm, giving the phrase the sense “a swarm of living creatures.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, used collectively as the cognate object of יִשְׁרְצוּ.
analysis.sense: Living creatures that swarm, taken collectively.

analysis.evidence: The feminine singular adjective חַיָּה ‘living’ modifies נֶפֶשׁ. Together they describe the creatures with which God commands the waters to swarm.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with feminine agreement here. No prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: חַיָּה agrees with the feminine singular noun נֶפֶשׁ and modifies it. Together they mean “a living creature” in the command for the waters to swarm with life.
In וְעוֹף יְעוֹפֵף ‘and let birds fly’, עוֹף is the collective subject of the singular verb יְעוֹפֵף. The flight over the earth identifies the group as birds.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ־ ‘and’ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The singular verb יְעוֹפֵף agrees with the collective subject עוֹף, “birds.” The phrase עַל הָאָרֶץ, “above the earth,” locates their flight. The parallel with יִשְׁרְצוּ, “let the waters swarm,” gives the verb its command force.
analysis.morphology: Polel imperfect, third person masculine singular, with jussive force. No attached preposition, conjunction, or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וְעוֹף יְעוֹפֵף עַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל takes הָאָרֶץ as its object and locates the birds’ flight over the earth.
In יְעוֹפֵף עַל הָאָרֶץ, the birds fly above the ground. The following phrase עַל פְּנֵי רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם locates their flight across the face of the sky.
analysis.morphology: הָ־ definite article + common noun, singular absolute

analysis.evidence: The second עַל introduces פְּנֵי רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם, “the face of the expanse of the heavens.” With יְעוֹפֵף, “let fly,” it describes the birds’ flight across that face.
פְּנֵי governs רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם, “the expanse of the heavens.” The phrase עַל פְּנֵי רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם describes birds flying across the visible face of the expanse.
analysis.morphology: Common-gender plural noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם, רְקִיעַ is in construct with הַשָּׁמָיִם. The birds fly across the face of the expanse of the heavens.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: The birds are to fly above the earth across the face of רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם, “the expanse of the sky.” Their flight identifies the visible sky overhead.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state.
